title: Gave Claude and Codex access to my Schwab account
author: purealgo
selftext:
I've traded options on thinkorswim for many years. Outside of simple backtests and trading signals, I was not interesting in automated trading. But, AI has finally gotten good enough to get involved.

A few 3rd party projects already connect AI agents to Schwab, but the ones I tried were bloated or a pain to set up. So I wrote my own connector (an MCP server). It installs as one small, fast program with nothing else to download.

What it does..

\- Reads your balances, positions, orders, and transaction history  
\- Pulls live quotes, option chains, price history, and market movers  
\- Keeps you logged in, so you only log in about once a week  
\- Can place trades on your behalf

It can't trade unless you turn trading on. By default it can only read your account and preview orders. If you enable trading, it can place real orders, so check every order before you approve it.

Setup takes a few minutes. You run one install command, create a free Schwab developer app, and log in. The README walks through each step.

Repo: [https://github.com/itsmostafa/schwab-mcp](https://github.com/itsmostafa/schwab-mcp)

It's free and open source, and Schwab has no part in it. I'm just sharing this for free. But any feedback is appreciated... thanks!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
The read only default with trading behind a flag is the right shape. The gap that bit us on a similar setup is the time between preview and approve: the chain the agent reasoned over is a snapshot, so if a person takes thirty seconds to read the order, the greeks that justified it are already stale.

Worth stamping every quote the agent pulls with its own timestamp and refusing to preview an order built on anything older than a few seconds. Does yours re-pull the chain at approval time, or approve against the original snapshot?

replies.author: purealgo
replies.body: Thanks for the advice! I'll go ahead and update this. I'll get it to pull quotes everytime before reasoning over quotes that quickly become stale.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
The one that bit us: fresh at the start of the reasoning still goes stale by the end if the plan runs a few steps. Putting the fetch time into the payload so the model can see the age beats assuming it is current.

Is your re-pull before the thinking or right before the order goes out?

replies.author: purealgo
replies.body:
Re-pulls right before order goes out. Here's what its doing so far: 

1. The agent calls get\_quotes, reasons for however long, and builds the order.

2. The agent calls place\_order.

3. The server fetches a fresh quote, with a 5s timeout. If it hits the timeout, order is rejected and never sent.

4. It checks the order against that quote.

5. If the order passes, the server sends it to Schwab right away. If it fails, the server returns a rejection with the live bid, ask and last price, so the agent can rebuild the order.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
The gap left after that is between your check and Schwab's ack, and the only thing bounding it is the order type. If the agent sends market orders, the fresh quote validates intent but not the fill.

Are you deriving a limit off the re-pulled quote, or passing through whatever the agent built?

replies.author: purealgo
replies.body: It passes the agent's order through untouched. It never sets a price of its own. By default it just refuses to send anything that isn't already price capped, so a market order can only slip through if you've explicitly turned that safety off.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Refusing anything without a price cap is the right default. The case I'd go test is a limit the agent prices at the far side of a wide spread, because that's a market order wearing a hat and it passes your check.
